catalog_quote: Se puede decir que el nomatsiguenga posee acento tonal, es decir que las palabras pueden tener ciertas vocales marcadas con un acento. La vocal acentuada se pronuncia con un tono bastante mas alto que las demas vocales de la palabra. La vocal acentuada no es siempre mas larga ni mas fuerte que las demas que aparecen en la palabra; en efecto, las vocales no acentuadas pueden pronunciarse con m&s fuerza (o mas intensidad) que la vocal acentuada. ... Puesto que la vocal acentuada se distingue principalmente por el tono alto, y no por la intensidad (mayor fuerza de la voz) o por la duracion, resulta mas correcto hablar de "acento tonal" que de "acento prosodico" o de "tono". Algunos pares de palabras difieren solamente por el acento tonal. sweep_summary: One works with stress in the title, already held by the project and now read in full: Apolinario Vilcarromero 2020 (UNMSM Licenciatura thesis, open PDF via Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú / etnolinguistica.org). It is squarely about word stress in Nomatsigenga nouns and contradicts the catalog's 'tonal' coding (Shaver 1996 dictionary appendix, 'acento tonal'): stress is a duration-cued metrical system in a left-edge two-syllable window (penult in 72% incl. all disyllables; antepenult/initial in 25% of trisyllables; final in 2 words), CVN codas weightless, H tone a separate non-obligatory system, hence 'nomatsigenga no es una lengua pitch accent' (p. 89). Recommend reclassification the catalog from 'tonal' to a stress language with a left two-syllable window (penult default, lexically antepenult), citing Apolinario 2020 as deciding source and retaining Shaver/Lawrence for the H-tone contrast. Lawrence 2013 (UT Austin MA report, stress statement pp. 15-17) remains unfetchable (CloudFront 403; archive.org unreachable) and is the one acquisition worth pursuing.

new_statements.quote: El patrón acentual que gobierna los nombres de la lengua nomatsigenga consiste en asignar el acento dentro una ventana de las dos primeras sílabas dentro de la palabra nominal. [...] El primer patrón consiste en acentuar la antepenúltima sílaba. El segundo patrón, el más frecuente, señala que se debe acentuar la penúltima sílaba. [...] Los correlatos fonéticos principales del acento nominal son la duración y la calidad vocálica. Por tanto, nomatsigenga no es una lengua pitch accent, pues no todas sus sílabas acentuadas portan un tono alto.
new_statements.translation: The stress pattern governing nouns in Nomatsigenga consists in assigning stress within a window of the first two syllables of the noun. [...] The first pattern stresses the antepenultimate syllable. The second pattern, the most frequent, stresses the penultimate syllable. [...] The main phonetic correlates of nominal stress are duration and vowel quality. Therefore Nomatsigenga is not a pitch-accent language, since not all of its stressed syllables carry a high tone.
new_statements.citation: Apolinario Vilcarromero, Rosa Beatriz. 2020. Acento nominal en nomatsigenga (arawak). Tesis de Licenciatura, Universidad Nacional Mayor de San Marcos, Lima. 114 pp.
new_statements.locator: Conclusiones, printed p. 89 = PDF p. 101 (supporting data: sec. 7.3 pp. 80-85, Tabla 45 p. 88, Tabla 18 p. 60)
new_statements.reading: First-hand acoustic and metrical study (72 nouns, 6 speakers) finds a genuine stress system, cued by duration and vowel quality, confined to the first two syllables of the noun: penultimate in 72% of words (all disyllables, most trisyllables), antepenultimate/initial in 25% of trisyllables, final in 2 words; CVN codas are weightless; the H-tone contrast reported by Shaver/Lawrence coexists but is not obligatory on the stressed syllable. This directly contradicts the catalog's 'tonal' (pitch accent) coding built on Shaver 1996's dictionary appendix, which had no phonetic backing. Caveats: nouns only, 2-3 syllable words only, Licenciatura thesis; the tone contrast itself is not denied.

readall_conflicts: Neither listed work could be opened, so no new first-hand statements were obtained; the overall reading stays with the existing first-hand statement (Apolinario 2020: duration-cued stress in a window of the first two syllables of the noun, penultimate in 72% of the 72 nouns and in all disyllables, antepenultimate in ~25% of trisyllables, H tone a separate non-obligatory system), which already contradicts the catalog's tonal/pitch accent coding built on Shaver 1996. One further disagreement is visible only second-hand: Apolinario (pp. 9-10) reports Lawrence 2013: 17 as analysing stress as disyllabic iambic feet with stress attracted by closed syllables carrying high tone (e.g. [a.'ro], i.e. final stress in disyllables), whereas Apolinario's own acoustic data put stress on the first syllable of every disyllable and find CVN codas weightless. Whether Lawrence's iambic claim is really final-oriented, and whether it covers nouns or only verbs, cannot be checked until the UT Austin PDF is obtained from a host that CloudFront does not block.

audit.recode_to: conflict (as used for Desano): Payne in Shaver 1996 = lexical pitch accent, H pitch only, no stress; Lawrence 2013 = lexical H/zero tone plus separate iambic stress; Apolinario 2020 (acoustic, 228 tokens) = stress cued by duration and vowel quality within the first two syllables of nouns, H tone a separate, under-described system, 'not pitch accent'. At minimum strike 'accent realized by high pitch, explicitly NOT by duration' / 'no stress rule of any kind' from the primary-stress rule/tone_note and add a caution; keep the lexical-tone component (all three sources accept unpredictable H placement and Shaver's minimal pairs).

The two later sources disagree

Nouns carry one stress inside a left-edge window of the first two syllables: Pattern 2 penultimate = 52/72 (72%; every disyllable is initial-stressed, 25 trisyllables CV.'CV.CV), Pattern 1 antepenultimate/initial in trisyllables = 18/72 (25%), Pattern 3 final = 2 words (3%). CVN syllables do not attract stress ('no generan peso silábico', p. 80); stress goes to the phonetically longest vowel (Tabla 45: syllable-boundary projection on heavy CV:, right-edge marking, head left).
